## How it works

- [statement] Solana sendTransaction returns the first transaction signature when the RPC accepts the signed transaction, without waiting for confirmation. Its documentation says success does not guarantee processing or confirmation and says the signature can be extracted before submission. (low confidence) — https://solana.com/docs/rpc/http/sendtransaction · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] Solana getTransaction looks up a transaction by signature at a requested commitment and returns null when it is not found or not confirmed there. Its documented response includes blockTime, metadata, slot and transaction data, with nullable fields. (low confidence) — https://solana.com/docs/rpc/http/gettransaction · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] Ethereum eth_getTransactionByHash documents transaction hash, sender and nonce, with null block hash/number fields while pending. Its lookup can return null when no transaction is found. (low confidence) — https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/apis/json-rpc/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] The cited Ethereum log response defines removed as true when a log was removed because of a chain reorganization. The response also carries transaction and block identities. (low confidence) — https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/apis/json-rpc/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] Bybit’s cited execution-history response documents order and execution identities, execution type/time, quantity, price/value, remaining quantity and fee-related fields when provided. It warns that executions with equal execution times can be sorted ambiguously and gives symbol-specific sequence guidance. (low confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/order/execution · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] Bybit’s Unified transaction log documents entry identity, time/type, instrument/category, currency, order/trade references, funding, trading fee, cash flow, balance change and cash balance fields. The documented funding sign distinguishes received from paid amounts, while positive trading fees mean expense and negative fees mean rebates. (low confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/account/transaction-log · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] In Bybit’s cited Unified transaction-log documentation, the fee-rate interpretation depends on the entry type, including settlement funding-rate conventions. USDC perpetual settlement can include funding and session settlement, so the funding and cash-flow fields are distinct. (low confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/account/transaction-log · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] The cited Prometheus Alertmanager documentation defines inhibition as suppressing notifications for certain alerts when specified other alerts are already firing. It describes silences as time-bounded muting: an incoming alert matching an active silence’s equality or regular-expression matchers receives no notification. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/alertmanager/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot monitor evidence and latency contracts

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The cited Solana transaction JSON structures describe pre/post native balances and token-balance records including account index, mint and token amount/decimals, with optional owner and program identity. Transaction metadata separately exposes fee and execution-error information. (low confidence) — https://solana.com/docs/rpc/json-structures · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] The historical RFC 2679 explains that source/destination clock synchronization error and clock resolution contribute uncertainty to one-way IP delay measurements. It separately requires accounting for uncertainty between software host timestamps and wire times. (low confidence) — https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2679 · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot monitor evidence and latency contracts
- [statement] In the cited OAuth Bearer specification, invalid_token includes an expired, revoked, malformed or otherwise invalid access token; insufficient_scope means the request needs greater privileges than the token supplies. These error meanings belong to that authentication scheme. (low confidence) — https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750 · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot monitor evidence and latency contracts

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The cited OAuth Bearer specification says a resource server should omit an error code when a request lacks authentication information, including an unsupported authentication method. Its missing-authentication example differs from the invalid_token error response. (low confidence) — https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750 · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot monitor evidence and latency contracts

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For recent-blockhash expiry checking, the Solana cookbook says to retain lastValidBlockHeight and poll confirmed block height until it exceeds that bound. It treats durable-nonce transaction confirmation separately. (low confidence) — https://solana.com/developers/cookbook/transactions/confirmation · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] Ethereum eth_getTransactionReceipt is unavailable for a pending transaction and documents block identity, execution status, gas used and effective gas price. Gas used is transaction gas consumption; effective gas price is the paid price per gas unit. (low confidence) — https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/apis/json-rpc/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] The cited Ethereum eth_sendTransaction documentation says an optional nonce permits overwriting a pending transaction that uses the same nonce. (low confidence) — https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/apis/json-rpc/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] The cited Bybit execution-history and Unified transaction-log endpoints document time filters and next-page cursors, with different default time windows. (medium confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/order/execution · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts · also: https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/account/transaction-log
- [statement] Bybit’s cited ticker documentation lists mark price, last traded price and index price as separate fields. Its positions response lists mark price and reported position leverage separately. (medium confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/market/tickers · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts · also: https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/position
- [statement] Bybit’s cited positions response describes cross-margin liquidation price as estimated and documents an empty liquidation-price value in portfolio margin mode or outside specified price bounds. It also returns an empty leverage field for portfolio margin mode. (low confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/position · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] Bybit’s cited positions response defines positionIMByMp and positionMMByMp as initial and maintenance margin calculated by mark price. It documents empty values for those fields in portfolio margin mode. (low confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/position · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] The cited StepSecurity article recommends not putting private keys in environment files for third-party tools and recommends hardware wallets or separate signing services. (low confidence) — https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-polymarket-bot-hides-in-hijacked-dev-protocol-github-org-and-steals-wallet-keys · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] Bybit’s cited Unified transaction log defines change = cashFlow + funding - fee and states that cashFlow excludes trading and funding fees. It defines cashBalance as wallet balance after a cash change; this is the documented entry-level cash relation. (low confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/account/transaction-log · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot chain execution and valuation contracts
- [statement] The cited Grafana Cloud IRM response documentation says silencing prevents notifications for a specified duration without resolving the issue. While the group is silenced, IRM records source firing and resolve signals but does not act on them. This is notification-handling state, not evidence that the underlying bot has recovered. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/respond-to-alerts/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot monitor evidence and latency contracts
- [statement] CCXT documents switching to an exchange sandbox only if the underlying exchange supports it, immediately after constructing the exchange and before any other call. The manual states that sandbox keys are not interchangeable with production keys. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/wiki/manual · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot monitor proposed drill and recovery oracles
- [statement] Within its firm-performance reporting scope, the GIPS handbook requires returns after transaction costs and permits estimated transaction costs only for portfolios whose actual transaction costs are not known. (low confidence) — https://www.gipsstandards.org/standards/gips-standards-for-firms/gips-standards-handbook-for-firms/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot performance and drift uncertainty contracts
- [statement] Evidently’s cited drift documentation requires nonempty reference/current columns and filters empty or infinite values for distribution drift. It says default drift tests do not react to increasing empty counts and recommends separate null-share tests. (low confidence) — https://docs.evidentlyai.com/metrics/explainer_drift · keywords: Crypto bot monitor reference and proposed validation contracts, Crypto bot performance and drift uncertainty contracts
